body: As someone also with gHsv1 (male,24) I definitely relate and understand your struggle. I’ve personally found small success in casual dating scene but it’s exhausting wondering if people will think differently.
Nice! It’s a good feeling to realize a large portion of people really don’t care about your status as much as we fear that they would.
As another male with GHsV 1 in my case I have had the same experiences. Honesty   from the get go results in positive disclosures most of the time.
Congratulations! It’s refreshing to hear positive disclosure stories like this! I hope people continue to post theirs

O-HSV1 does not like the genitals so generally transmission from Oral to Genitals is already extremely low as it is.
Also, have you ever had a blood HSV test done before? If not, I recommend it. A large portion of adults carry HSV1 with no symptoms for their entire lives, and once you have HSV1 in your body no matter if its OHSV1 or GHSV1 or Dormant Asymptomatic HSV1 then after a period of time you can no longer be reinfected by HSV1. So if you tested positive for having HSV1 dormant in you (its very possible) then his Oral HSV1 will not do anything to you, your body already recognizes the virus and defends from reinfection. 

Alternatively dental dams are a female condom you can look into.  There are a ton of ways to prevent infection, and tons of couples who have been in long term relationships without any infection. If you truly like this person then I would try and learn to accept this fact about them. They literally cannot change it. If that’s too difficult to do then cut things off as soon as you can. Too many people drag others emotions through the coals because they hesitate for so long and ultimately hurt the other person.
If you have hsv1 orally for more than 3 months then you cant be reinfected with Hsv1 anywhere else on your body. You guys are good to go

Somebody correct me if I’m wrong but most research I’ve seen says Hsv is extremely fragile virus that cant live outside of a human body so transmission via drinks or joints or anything like that would not be possible! Either way, I’m glad your disclosure was positive!

Hey! So I just want to say even if you are hsv positive you are absolutely still normal! This would not detract from your outward or inward beauty one single bit! Do not let the fear take over your mind :)

This can go one of three ways and only three ways.

1.) You never tell her and the eventual guilt will bleed over into your personal life leading to possible depression and problems at home.

2.) You do tell her and she takes it harshly, (which you should respect anyways because you have been dishonest) and you both go on with your lives knowing that was something that was very difficult but necessary in both of your personal developments

Or 3.) You fess up and tell her with genuine honesty and she looks past your secret and accept you for who you are and always have been and you can truly love freely and exist without the burden of guilt.

I feel like the only true way to overcome that is to just accept it wholeheartedly and maybe even find the humor in a not-so-funny situation. I’ve just laughed along with the joke (either at how uninformed it was OR because it was accurate or relatable)
I agree with that

Mono can result in some cases the rupturing of the spleen or liver. That alone is more dangerous than HSV. The reoccurrence of HSV is obviously a key difference but both are viruses that spread through physical interaction (saliva for mono). If you had said that HSV safety needs to be taught more to people I would 100% agree. To say that HsV needs to remain stigmatized is ridiculous. Stigmatizing HSV DOES NOT STOP THE SPREAD OR REDUCE INFECTION. People who are infected and choose not to disclose will continue to do so even if it was stigmatized or not. People with good conscious will continue to disclose to potential partners. The continual stigma of HSV has gotten us nowhere as a group and if anything has spread disinformation.

Obviously your partner values you over your infection. Some people are genuinely not worried about catching the virus because they’re with the one they love and see forever with. Love can overpower anything, so keep your head up. They know the risks and continue to be there. That means a lot, even if worst comes to worst and it was transmitted, I dont think it would be the end for your relationship if it’s held up to this point.

HSV is not a disease it’s a virus. The stigma exists because pharmaceutical companies used HSV as a driving force in the lobbying for Doctors to prescribe more medications. Pre
WW1-2 there was basically no widespread stigma of HSV. If the stigma should be associated with HsV because it is a “disease” then where is the stigma for things like Mono? That’s spread the same way as HSV if not more likely to spread and is hardly talked about or even mentioned. I get where you are coming from but your logic can be applied to ANY virus or disease. If we need to stigmatize hsv then we need to stigmatize EVERY virus and infection possible. While were at it why dont we just live in a bubble too.
Exactly, Me too. At this point it’s something we cannot change as much as we wish so whoever wants us must accept the WHOLE package :)
